review: 1:3–1:4 and 3:3 אֲהַבְתָּנוּ / שִׂמַּחְתָּנוּ — the Arabic repetitions (أَحْبَبْتَنَا, أَسْعَدْتَنَا) are kept, including the same suffix, because the hymn's argument is the Father's single act in the Son.
2:3 בִּבְנְךָ אִמַּצְתָּנוּ — 'by Your Son You made us sons'; אִמֵּץ is the biblical verb of making firm, used here for the adoption because the direct hiph'il of בנה would read as 'build'.
3:2 דְּבֵקוּת לָנֶצַח — 'cleaving forever'; the Arabic الْتِصَاق is the noun, and דְּבֵקוּת is its liturgical Hebrew equivalent (Deut 11:22 uses the verb דָּבַק).

3:4 נֶצַח עוֹלָמִים — 'the eternity of eternities', for الْآبُ الصَّمَد; the Arabic الصَّمَد is the Qur'anic 'eternal, self-sufficient', and נֶצַח עוֹלָמִים is the biblical superlative that carries it.
